conclusions: Canonical thread id is supplied from trusted conversation to the optional repository capability. Namespace/thread key separates repositories; repository identity is retained and mismatch rejected. Production namespace construction remains a wiring responsibility.
Same-thread queue spans open through close, while different thread keys open independently. One manager under the existing host lease is the intended ownership boundary.

Accepted revision advances through durable prepared intent then exact old-ref CAS then durable acknowledgement. Restart only recognizes the exact already-advanced produced ref; unapplied/ambiguous prepared state refuses replay. Paid-call journal remains separate authority.

Configured storage/revision limits fail closed. These are acceptance limits, not hard process/disk sandbox claims; initial clone resources and retained interrupted drafts remain operational considerations.
Validation capability is optional at this source-layer API; production must wire the isolated revision validator before enabling generated-code acceptance.
